response.draft:
Slide 1: Cogline Bike Works: FY2027 Evening Cohort
A request to the Ostrander Family Fund
Request: $60,000 toward a $96,000 evening apprenticeship cohort
Granger Street, Pellam Ridge
Results are from the FY2026 Annual Program Report (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026)

Slide 2: What We Do
Nonprofit bike repair shop and apprenticeship program on Granger Street in Pellam Ridge
Adults who are out of work or underemployed train in a paid, 16-week apprenticeship
Apprentices earn a stipend while they train
Training covers entry-level bike shop skills: wheel truing, brake and drivetrain service, hub overhaul, frame inspection, customer intake, basic shop math
Rebuilt bikes are sold at low prices or given free to residents who need a way to get to work or school
Staff of three: executive director, lead instructor, half-time shop manager

Slide 3: FY2026 Results
Apprentices enrolled: 26 (up from 18 in FY2025, +44%)
Completed all 16 weeks: 19 (up from 12, +58%)
Completion rate: 73% (up from 67%)
Employed within 90 days: 14 of 19 (up from 8 of 12)
Bikes refurbished: 482 (up from 310, +55%)
Bikes given free to residents: 205 (up from 140, +46%)
Shop earned income: $58,600 (up from $41,200, +42%)
Most of the growth came from one change: running two overlapping cohorts, starting eight weeks apart, beginning September 2025

Slide 4: Employment After 90 Days: 14 of 19 (74%)
9 hired by bike shops or bike rental and fleet operators in the county
3 hired in related mechanical trades: small-engine, appliance repair, forklift maintenance
2 hired by Cogline as part-time shop assistants
Median starting wage $17.25 an hour, compared with $13.10 reported at intake
Caveat: this is a small group. One graduate moves the rate by about five points
Caveat: 7 of the 14 placements were confirmed by an employer. The other 7 are self-reported by the graduate
Caveat: we do not have one-year retention data for FY2026 graduates yet
FY2025 one-year check: 7 of the 8 employed at 90 days were still working. That is one cohort of 12, not a trend yet
Starting in FY2027, we will ask every graduate for employer contact consent at graduation

Slide 5: From a Graduate
Dariel M., spring cohort graduate, now works the service desk at a shop in the county seat
"I came in thinking I'd learn to fix flats. What I actually learned was how to look at a problem, write down what's wrong, and give somebody a straight price. That's the part they hired me for."
482 bikes rebuilt in FY2026: 277 sold through the shop, mostly $60 to $180, and 205 given free
Free bikes went to residents referred by the adult education center, two family shelters, and the county reentry office
Every free bike goes out with a lock, lights, and a fitted helmet

Slide 6: FY2026 Finances
Operating expenses: $312,400
Apprentice stipends $118,800 (38%) and staff salaries and benefits $121,500 (39%)
Rent and utilities $28,800 (9%); parts, tools, and safety gear $24,600 (8%); insurance, accounting, and admin $18,700 (6%)
Cost per enrolled apprentice fell from $13,900 to $12,015
Revenue: $318,000, with a $5,600 surplus added to the operating reserve
Tallis County Workforce Board $120,000 (38%); Ferncliff Community Foundation $75,000 (24%); shop earned income $58,600 (18%); individual donors and Spring Gear-Up Ride $44,400 (14%); Northway Cycle Supply $20,000 (6%)

Slide 7: The Need: An Evening Cohort
Waitlist at the end of FY2026: 31 people
22 of the 31 said they could only attend in the evening
Most already have daytime jobs, often part-time or with shifting schedules, and can't leave them for a weekday program
Evening cohort: Monday to Thursday, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m., for 20 weeks, matching the day program's hours
Planned start: February 2027
Total enrollment grows from 26 to 36 apprentices

Slide 8: Evening Cohort Cost and Our Request
Second instructor (1.0 FTE, salary and benefits): $52,000
Stipends for 10 evening apprentices: $30,000
Added tools, workstands, and safety gear: $8,500
Evening utilities and building access: $5,500
Total evening cohort cost: $96,000
Already committed by the Tallis County Workforce Board: $36,000
Remaining gap: $60,000. This is our request to the Ostrander Family Fund
Full FY2027 budget, including the evening cohort: $408,400
FY2027 targets: 36 enrolled, at least 26 completing, at least 70% of completers employed within 90 days, at least half of placements confirmed directly with an employer
